content.text:
PR #2 is merged into `main` as `0fa089b`. It went through the **full audit route, not Light**, and the verdict was **clean**.

**What changed:** the index page welcome text now reads "Welcome to Throwaway Rc3" in English and "ようこそ、Throwaway Rc3へ" in Japanese.

**Audit:** `code-audit-frontend` was the only reviewer this change needed. It took 3 rounds:
- **Round 1:** a full review found one Minor issue. I had typed the project name straight into the welcome text, so the fixer changed it to read the name from `meta.siteName`.
- **Round 2:** this one started as a Light review, but it escalated to a full review. It found three Minor issues:
  - **Fixed:** nothing tested the welcome text, so the fixer added a check to the index page's Storybook story.
  - **Filed as tech-debt issue #3:** the index page title still has the project name typed in. That file isn't part of this PR, so it wasn't changed here.
  - **Accepted and noted in the PR body:** the `welcome` string sits with the shared strings instead of the index page's own strings. It was already there before this change, and moving it would be a bigger refactor than a copy change justifies.
- **Round 3:** a full review with zero findings. The `GAIA-Audit` status was posted after this round.

**Things worth knowing:**
- **The audit changed more than the two strings.** The merged change also includes the `meta.siteName` lookup and the new story check.
- **The merge was blocked once.** A second merge check requires a quality verdict on any changed test, so the new story check needed one. The reviewer agent judged it worth keeping, but its first attempt couldn't save its result because the worktree's safety guard blocked the shared folder. It succeeded on one retry with a different file location, and I recorded the verdict. This is a gap in the GAIA tooling worth fixing: that reviewer can't write its output from inside a worktree.
